### iliad-104 (16.477–568)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τοῦ δ’ οὐχ ἅλιον βέλος ἔκφυγε χειρός (16.480; the same line as 5.18, so the published English of 5.18 is reused, not a new rendering) | "and from his hand the shaft did not escape in vain" | "and his shaft did not leave his hand in vain" | "missed", "was not wasted", "flew from the hand" (that is 14.407, a different line); ἅλιος "in vain" as at 4.498 (not ἅλιος "of the sea") |
| φρένες (bodily, 16.481, 16.504) | "midriffs" | "midriff" (+ note: which organs about the heart are meant is not known) | "wits" (reserved for φρένες as the mind, table 10.10), "lungs", "diaphragm" (each decides the organ), "heart" (reserved for κῆρ, ἦτορ, κραδίη); follows the Odyssey table’s φρένες of the body, "the midriff" (9.301), with the plural kept in `l` |
| ἔρχαται (16.481) | "are shut about" | "is shut about" | "lie around", "enclose"; perfect passive of εἴργω "shut in", Ionic -αται |
| ἁδινὸν κῆρ (16.481) | "the thronging heart" | "the thronging heart" (+ note: what ἁδινός says of a heart is not known) | "thick" (the first draft; the Odyssey table has ἀδινὸν κῆρ "thronging heart", 19.516, and ἁδινάων "thronging" of bees, 2.87), "throbbing", "strong", "stout" |
| Λυκίων ἀγὸς ἀσπιστάων (16.490, 16.541) | "leader of the Lycians, the shield-bearers" | "the leader of the Lycian shield-bearers" | "chief of the shielded Lycians", "captain"; ἀγός "leader" (table 4.519), ἀσπιστής "shield-bearer" (table 8.155) |
| κτεινόμενος μενέαινε (16.491) | "being killed, was eager" | "as he was being killed, was full of eagerness" (+ note: the verb has no object) | "raged", "strove", "was furious" (each supplies an object or a feeling the Greek does not state); μενεαίνω "be eager" (table 4.32) |
| Γλαῦκε πέπον πολεμιστά (16.492) | "Glaucus, good one, warrior" | "Glaucus, my good fellow, warrior" (+ note: meaning of πέπον not known) | "dear friend", "comrade"; follows the table’s ὦ πέπον "O good one" / "my good fellow" (9.252) |
| Λυκίων ἡγήτορας ἄνδρας (16.495, 16.532) | "the leader-men of the Lycians" | "the leaders of the Lycians" | "the Lycian captains", "the leading men" (drops one of the two nouns in `l`); ἡγήτωρ "leader" (table 2.79), ἄνδρας in apposition |
| πάντῃ ἐποιχόμενος Σαρπηδόνος ἀμφιμάχεσθαι (16.496, 16.533, same words, same English) | "everywhere going to and fro, around Sarpedon to fight" | "going all about to fight around Sarpedon" | "going about" in `l` (the first draft), "round and round", "hither and thither", "defend"; ἐποίχομαι "go to and fro" in `l` and "go about" in `i`, as in the table’s ἐποιχομένη (5.720) |
| κατηφείη καὶ ὄνειδος (16.498) | "a shame and a reproach" | "a shame and a reproach" (+ note: κατηφείη from κατηφής "downcast"; shame felt or shame caused is not decided) | "disgrace", "a cause of dishonour"; ὄνειδος "reproach" as in the table’s ὀνείδεα (3.242) |
| τέλος θανάτοιο κάλυψεν (16.502) | "the end of death covered" | "the end that death brings covered" | "the shadow of death", "the cloud of death"; follows the table’s τέλος θανάτοιο (5.553) and κάλυψεν "covered" |
| ἕλκος … τόδε καρτερόν (16.517, 16.523) | "this strong wound" (at 517 the word order gives "a wound I have, this strong one" in `l`) | "this severe wound" | "mighty", "grievous" (kept for ἀργαλέος, 11.812 and 16.528), "terrible"; καρτερός "strong" in `l`, "severe" in `i` for a wound |
| ὀξείῃς ὀδύνῃσιν ἐλήλαται (16.518) | "with sharp pains has been driven" | "is beset on every side with sharp pains" (+ note: the picture is not clear) | "racked", "pierced through", "gripped"; ἐλαύνω "drive" in `l`, the sense only in `i` |
| βαρύθει … ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ (16.519) | "is heavy under it" | "is weighed down by it" | "aches", "hangs heavy"; βαρύθω "be heavy" |
| ἀνὴρ ὤριστος (16.521) | "a man, the best" | "the best of men" | "the noblest man", "the bravest of men"; ὤριστος is ὁ ἄριστος (crasis) |
| κοίμησον δ’ ὀδύνας (16.524) | "put to sleep the pains" | "put my pains to sleep" | "still", "lull", "soothe"; κοιμάω "put to sleep" |
| νέκυι κατατεθνηῶτι (16.526, 16.565, same words, same English) | "the dead man, him who has died" | "the dead man" | "the corpse" (kept for νεκρός), "the body"; follows the Odyssey table’s νεκύων κατατεθνηώτων "of the dead, of those who had died" (11.37), νέκυς "the dead" |
| εἲς / εἰς (second singular of εἰμί, 16.515, 16.538) | "you are" | "you are" (and "have" with a perfect participle: λελασμένος εἰς "you have forgotten") | "into" (the preposition is a different word); the note says what the form is |
| ἀποφθινύθουσι with θυμόν (16.540) | "are wasting away their life" | "are wasting their lives away" | "are dying off" (kept for the intransitive use at 5.643), "perishing" (kept for ἀπόλλυμαι) |
| νεμεσσήθητε θυμῷ (16.544) | "feel resentment in your heart" | "feel resentment in your hearts" | "be indignant", "feel indignation" (the first draft; the table turns "be indignant with" down for νεμεσίζομαι and keeps νεμεσσάω "feel resentment", 2.222–223, 2.296, 4.413), "be ashamed", "have shame" (αἰδώς); the note says the feeling is nearer to righteous indignation |
| ἀεικίσσωσι δὲ νεκρόν (16.545; ἀεικισσαίμεθ’, 16.559) | "treat unseemly the corpse" | "abuse his corpse" / "abuse him" | "mutilate", "outrage", "dishonour"; ἀεικής "unseemly" (1.341), from which the verb is made |
| ἄσχετον, οὐκ ἐπιεικτόν (16.549) | "unrestrainable, not yielding" | "unrestrainable and unyielding" | "unbearable", "not to be borne"; follows the table’s ἀάσχετον οὐκ ἐπιεικτόν (5.892–893) |
| ἕρμα πόληος (16.549) | "a prop of the city" | "the prop of their city" | "bulwark", "defence" (kept for ἕρκος), "anchor"; the table’s ἕρμα "prop" (2.154, 4.117) |
| ἀριστεύεσκε μάχεσθαι (16.551) | "used to be the best at fighting" | "used to be the best among them at fighting" | "excelled", "was the champion", "was always the best" (the first draft); the published English of the same words (6.460, 11.744, 16.291 in the shipped parts): "used to be the best at fighting"; ἀριστεύω "be the best" (table 6.208), iterative -εσκε "used to" |
| Μενοιτιάδεω Πατροκλῆος λάσιον κῆρ (16.554, the heart as subject) | "of Menoetius’-son Patroclus the shaggy heart" | "the shaggy heart of Patroclus, son of Menoetius" (the subject, first in `i` as at 2.851) | "the stout heart", "the brave heart"; follows the table’s λάσιον κῆρ "the shaggy heart" (2.851), the phrase names the man by his heart |
| νύκτ’ ὀλοήν … ὀλοὸς πόνος (16.567–568) | "a night baneful" … "a baneful toil" | "a baneful night" … "the baneful toil of fighting" | "deadly", "dreadful", "destructive" (kept for οὐλόμενος, ἀΐδηλος); ὀλοός "baneful" as in the table (3.133) |
| ἀμύνεσθαι (16.556, middle, no object) | "to defend yourselves" | "to defend yourselves" | "to ward off" (the active verb takes a thing warded off), "to ward off the enemy" (supplies an object); ἀμύνω in the middle is "defend oneself" (the glossary), and ἀλέξασθαι at 562 is "defend themselves" |
